The '''2024–25 Bundesliga''' was the 62nd season of the [[Bundesliga]], Germany's premier men's [[Association football|football]] competition. The season began on 23 August 2024 and concluded on 17 May 2025. [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]] were the defending champions.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Stafford-Bloor |first=Sebastian |date=2024-07-04 |title=Leverkusen to begin Bundesliga title defence with trip to Gladbach |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5616113/2024/07/04/bundesliga-fixture-list-2024-25/ |access-date=2026-08-25 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

On 4 May 2025, [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] were crowned Bundesliga champions for a record 33rd time (34th title overall) with two matches to spare following Bayer Leverkusen's 2–2 draw with [[SC Freiburg]], reclaiming the league title after a third-place finish in the previous season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Bayern Munich win 2024/25 Bundesliga title!|url=https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/bayern-munich-win-2024-25-title-kane-kompany-alonso-leverkusen-31866|date=4 May 2025|access-date=4 May 2025|publisher=Bundesliga}}</ref>

==Season overview==
The season began on 23 August 2024, and went into the winter break after the 15th matchday on 22 December. With the 16th matchday, the season continued on 10 January 2025. The final 34th matchday was scheduled for 17 May 2025.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.dfl.de/de/aktuelles/rahmenterminkalender-saison-2024-25/|title=Rahmenterminkalender für die Saison 2024/25: Bundesliga-Auftakt am 23. August 2024 – 2. Bundesliga startet am 2. August 2024|website=DFL.de |publisher=[[Deutsche Fußball Liga]] |date=27 October 2023|access-date=25 February 2024|language=de}}</ref><ref name="calendar">{{cite web |url=https://media.dfl.de/sites/2/2023/10/Rahmenterminkalender-2024_25-1.pdf|title=Rahmenterminkalender 2024/2025 |website=DFL.de |publisher=[[Deutsche Fußball Liga]] |date=27 October 2023|access-date=25 February 2024|language=de}}</ref>

The regular season was played as a [[round-robin tournament]]. Each team played a total of 34 matches, half at home and half away.

The fixtures were announced on 4 July 2024.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.kicker.de/bundesliga-spielplan-2024-25-bayern-startet-in-wolfsburg-1036020/artikel|title=Bundesliga-Spielplan 2024/25: Bayern startet in Wolfsburg|website=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]]|date=4 July 2024|access-date=4 July 2024|language=de}}</ref>

A total of 18 teams participate in the 2024–25 edition of the Bundesliga, 16 of which competed in the league campaign during the [[2023–24 Bundesliga|previous season]], while the remaining two were promoted from the [[2023–24 2. Bundesliga|2. Bundesliga]].

Holstein Kiel made its Bundesliga debut, making it the 58th different Bundesliga club and the first club from [[Schleswig-Holstein]], and returning to the German top flight after 60 years of absence. The club also replaced [[Hansa Rostock]] as the northernmost club in league history.<ref>{{cite news|title=Holstein Kiel promoted to the Bundesliga for first time!|url=https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/holstein-kiel-promoted-from-second-tier-for-first-time-27235|date=11 May 2024|access-date=11 May 2024|website=Bundesliga}}</ref> 

[[FC St. Pauli]] returned to the Bundesliga after a thirteen-year absence.<ref>{{cite news|title=Nach 13 Jahren: Der FC St. Pauli ist zurück in der Bundesliga!|url=https://www.bundesliga.com/de/bundesliga/news/fc-st-pauli-aufstieg-bundesliga-fabian-hurzeler-27162|date=13 May 2024|access-date=13 May 2024|website=Bundesliga|language=de}}</ref> For the first time ever, FC St. Pauli plays in a season at a higher level than [[Hamburg derby|local rivals]] [[Hamburger SV]].
